problem: On the live surface the operator selected 33 sources, chose ONE disposition and wrote ONE rationale, and the system refused the whole act: "33 sources exceeds the 25-source batch limit. This is refused rather than truncated: a partially applied batch that reported success would leave some sources decided and some not, with no record of where it stopped. Split the selection." The operator's verdict: "technically honest but operationally poor. It has detected the constraint. It has not solved the operator's problem."
observedFailure: A single governed intent — one disposition, one rationale, 33 subjects — was refused because of a backend batch size the operator has no reason to know exists.
The remedy was projected onto the operator ("Split the selection") although the system held every fact needed to perform it: 33 selected, limit 25, one disposition, one rationale.

There is no constitutional difference between admitting 33 sources in one batch and in two — the governed outcome, the receipts and the disclosure are identical — so the split was pure execution mechanics surfaced as operator workflow.
rootCauses: An implementation limit was treated as a constitutional boundary. Refusal-rather-than-truncation is the correct posture for a limit that would corrupt the record; it is the wrong posture for a limit the executor can simply plan around.
The executor could refuse and could succeed, but could not SEGMENT — so the only honest thing it could do with 33 was decline, and honesty became the ceiling on capability.
resolution: Recorded the operator-worded invariant: implementation constraints that do not alter constitutional intent shall be absorbed by the system rather than projected onto the operator.

The refusal-not-truncation reasoning is PRESERVED, not weakened: a partially applied batch reporting success would still be a defect. What changes is that the executor plans the segmentation instead of asking the operator to.
Enforcement point is being built in parallel by the Track 2 agent (executor-side batching). Recorded as PENDING rather than claimed.
rejectedApproaches: Truncate to the first 25 and report success — the original refusal is right about this: it would leave some sources decided and some not, with no record of where it stopped.
Raise the batch limit — moves the cliff without removing it, and the next operator meets it at 51.

Keep the refusal and improve its wording — the message was already accurate. The defect is not that it explained itself badly; it is that it asked the operator to do arithmetic the system had already done.
Make the split an explicit operator choice ("split into two batches?") — a confirmation for a decision with no constitutional content is still projected work.

incidentRefs: Operator live-surface report, 2026-08-03 — Track 2 Stage 2 bulk admission, 33 selected against a 25-source limit
